content:
Bloomberg reports that despite Apple accidentally leaking a video demonstrating its visual intelligence feature for AirPods, the product is still "on track for a 2027 release." Here are the details.

"Product challenges still need to be resolved"

Earlier this week, Apple accidentally included a video demonstrating the visual intelligence feature for AirPods in the macOS 26.7 candidate release.

A few days before the video was released, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman wrote in his Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been developing an AirPods variant equipped with cameras under the codename B798. I previously reported that the device was originally scheduled for a 2026 launch, then delayed to 2027. However, Apple is also developing another version under the codename B790 (Apple has previously developed competing versions of the same product in parallel internally). This B790 device appears to be further along in development: its product code has appeared in iOS 27, and it has been listed on Apple's internal roadmap, with a possible launch as early as this year.

Given that Apple accidentally included the related video in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, and with the company's expected iPhone launch event early next month drawing near, the B790 device appears to have a chance of being announced at that event.

However, Gurman now reports that although the leaked materials led some to believe the product could arrive sooner, Apple's "plans to sell AirPods with cameras are still on track for 2027."

The report stated:

Finally, Gurman noted that the recent leaks have further intensified controversy surrounding the device, with some users opposing AirPods with cameras on privacy grounds. But he also pointed out that these cameras will be low-resolution sensors, not intended for taking photos or recording video, but rather for "scanning the surrounding environment and providing contextual information for the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Whether this can quell criticism of the product—some have mockingly called it "pervert headphones"—remains to be seen next year.
